identity.referent: github.com/openclaw/openclaw — the open-source personal AI assistant / self-hosted Gateway by Peter Steinberger and the community, stewarded by the OpenClaw Foundation (MIT; repo created 2025-11-24; CLI `openclaw`; config ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json)
identity.scope_note: OpenClaw is NOT itself a coding agent: it is a personal-assistant gateway/runtime whose own native tools (exec, read, write, edit, apply_patch, browser, messaging) execute on the host, and which can host or drive coding harnesses (Claude, Codex, local models) as plugins. This adapter assesses OpenClaw's OWN native tool/exec boundary only, never the boundary of a harness it hosts.

ambiguous: two documented generations of the exec-policy surface: tools.exec.security+ask (official security guide, read directly) vs unified tools.exec.mode incl. an 'auto' automatic reviewer (community-mirrored docs + THIRD-PARTY) — which generation a pinned version implements is unknown and must be resolved before adapter code is written
hosted coding-harness plugins (Claude/Codex inside OpenClaw) and ACP coding sessions have their own boundaries — they are not OpenClaw's Decision layer and are out of scope for this manifest
gateway/node pairing approvals and DM pairing are trigger authorization, not the Approval layer for tool execution
layer_vocabulary.notes: IDENTITY: PINNED to github.com/openclaw/openclaw (see the top-level identity field for the full pin, basis, and excluded same-name candidates). rules (the Decision layer): tools.allow/tools.deny (deny always wins), tools.profile base allowlists, group:* shorthands, tools.byProvider, per-agent agents.list[].tools overrides; exec security/ask pair plus the host-local binary allowlist in ~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json with stricter-of-two precedence (file details THIRD-PARTY, partly corroborated by the official security guide). Granularity is tool/binary, NEVER argv: allowing a binary allows all of its arguments. approval (the Approval layer): exec ask modes (off/on-miss/always, or unified ask/auto), allow-once/allow-always/deny prompts, askFallback, tools.elevated escape-hatch gating; the 'auto' automatic reviewer is STOCHASTIC — an Approval-layer mechanism, never a decision oracle. sandbox (part of the Effect layer): agents.defaults.sandbox mode off/non-main/all, scope agent/session/shared, backend docker/ssh/openshell, workspaceAccess none/ro/rw, Docker network none by default; openclaw sandbox explain is the documented inspector. effect (the Effect layer — observed outcome): host execution by default, sandbox backends when enabled, node hosts as remote execution surface; NO live effect has been observed by this programme.

measurement_route_evidence: No vendor-confirmed offline checker is documented, but tool allow/deny (deny-wins), profiles/groups, sandbox configuration, and the exec security/ask + host binary-allowlist surface are documented precisely enough to compute evaluations at tool/binary granularity — labelled evaluation, never interrogation; argument-level questions serialize as unknown. (INFERENCE on DOC+THIRD-PARTY)

policy_ingestion.defaults: Default (DOC, security guide): host exec security="full", ask="off" — commands run without approval prompts; sandbox mode off (tools run on the host for the main session). No-match has no single rule: it depends on the configured exec mode (allowlist-mode no-match approx silent deny; ask-mode no-match approx prompt; full mode has no match concept). Unknowns serialize as unknown with layer attribution, never as allow.
policy_ingestion.surface: openclaw.json tools: { profile, allow[], deny[], alsoAllow[], byProvider, exec: { security|mode, ask }, elevated: { enabled, allowFrom }, fs: { workspaceOnly } }; agents.defaults.sandbox: { mode, scope, backend, workspaceAccess, docker.* }; host-local exec-approvals.json: { version, defaults: { security, ask, askFallback }, agents: { <id>: { security, ask, allowlist: [{ pattern }] } } }

spike_answers.a_native_oracle: NO (DOC-level; no install was permitted, so no REPRO reproduction backs this negative). No per-command check/evaluate/test entrypoint is documented in the primary sources read. Documented inspectors display state, not hypothetical decisions: openclaw security audit audits a config for footguns; openclaw sandbox explain reports effective sandbox mode and tool policy; openclaw approvals get / openclaw exec-policy show (THIRD-PARTY-reported) display requested policy, host approvals file, and effective merged result. None evaluates a command against a policy offline.
spike_answers.b_documented_semantics: YES, narrowly — at tool and binary granularity only, confidence low. Documented precisely: tools.allow/deny with deny-always-wins, profile base allowlists, group:* shorthands, per-agent and per-provider overrides, fail-closed empty allowlist (DOC); sandbox modes/scope/backends/workspaceAccess and Docker network-none default (DOC); exec security/ask defaults and hardened baseline (DOC). Exec-approvals file format, stricter-of-two precedence, and binary-path allowlist matching (allowing a binary allows all of its arguments) are THIRD-PARTY summaries of vendor docs, partly corroborated by the official security guide. Ceilings: NO documented argument-pattern rules for exec, so argument-shaped invariants are unknown at this layer; the vendor itself states exec approvals do not semantically model interpreter loader paths; compound-chain semantics unestablished in primary sources; the auto reviewer's decisions are stochastic; two documented generations of the exec surface (security+ask vs unified mode) are unresolved at any pinned version.
spike_answers.c_surface_record: Not applicable; harness uses the reconstructed route (narrow, low confidence). Defaults recorded in the assessment anyway: sandbox off, host exec security="full" / ask="off", DM pairing, Gateway as control plane.
